answer.worked: $[-3,5)$. Include $-3$ and exclude $5$: draw a closed point at $-3$, an open point at $5$, and join them.
Both endpoints are closed, so both are included: $-1\le x\le3$, or $[-1,3]$.
$(2,\infty)$. Exclude $2$: draw an open point at $2$ and a ray to the right. Infinity always has a round bracket.
$(-\infty,3]$. Include $3$: draw a closed point at $3$ and a ray to the left.
$x<4$. The round bracket excludes $4$, and the interval extends left without bound. Draw an open point at $4$ and a ray to the left.
$x\ge5$. The square bracket includes $5$, and the interval extends right without bound. Draw a closed point at $5$ and a ray to the right.
The open point excludes $-2$ and the ray extends left: $x<-2$, or $(-\infty,-2)$.
$(-\infty,1)\cup[3,\infty)$. Draw a leftward ray with an open point at $1$ and a rightward ray with a closed point at $3$. The union joins the two alternatives.
$(-\infty,-1]\cup[2,\infty)$. Both finite endpoints are included. Draw a closed point at $-1$ with a leftward ray and a closed point at $2$ with a rightward ray.
$(-4,-1]\cup[3,\infty)$. Join an open point at $-4$ to a closed point at $-1$. Also draw a closed point at $3$ with a rightward ray. Infinity is excluded.
